// diagnostic

E0151

`{state}` is not a declared state of `{type}`.

What

`{state}` is not a declared state of `{type}`.

Why

Typestate (D-STATE-HOME1=A): `struct {type} { state { … } }` defines the valid state labels; a name not in that set is likely a typo — a phantom state no transition can reach.

Fix

Correct the spelling, or add the name to the `state { … }` section inside `struct {type}`.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0151: tests/ui/typestate_unknown_state.stderr.

Error [E0151]: `Stuffed` is not a declared state of `Crate`
  --> tests/ui/typestate_unknown_state.jet:13:5
    |
 13 |     #State(Stuffed) fn get(self) Int -> { return self.data }
    |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: typestate (D-STATE-HOME1=A): `struct Crate { state { … } }` defines the valid state labels; `Stuffed` is not among them — a typo here would silently create a phantom state that no transition reaches
 Fix: add `Stuffed` to the `state { … }` section inside `struct Crate`, or correct the spelling
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0151

Error [E0150]: `get` needs `Crate` in state `Stuffed`, but `b` is in state `Full`
  --> tests/ui/typestate_unknown_state.jet:18:13
    |
 18 |     print(b.get())
    |             ^^^
 Why: typestate (D-STATE1): `get` is only valid in state `Stuffed`; calling it in `Full` is the out-of-order-events bug it prevents
 Fix: transition `b` into state `Stuffed` before calling `get`
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E0150
